## Summary

**What I found:**

| Evidence | Detail |
|---|---|
| Pod status | `ledger-queue-0` — **Pending**, no node assigned |
| Scheduler message | *"8 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict"* |
| Volume | `local-pv-ip-10-0-7-21-nvme1` — a local NVMe PV with `nodeAffinity: kubernetes.io/hostname In [ip-10-0-7-21.ec2.internal]` (the dead node) |
| PVC reclaim policy | **Delete** |
| Data at risk | Redis AOF log (`--appendonly yes`) containing unacknowledged settlement messages |

**Root cause:** `ledger-queue-0` uses a `local`-type PersistentVolume, which carries a hard nodeAffinity constraint pinning it exclusively to the failed node `ip-10-0-7-21` [cite: concepts/storage/volumes#local-0, cite: concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#node-affinity-0]. The scheduler correctly refuses to place the pod on any of the 8 healthy nodes because none of them satisfy that affinity. The pod cannot move until either the failed node returns, or the volume is replaced.

**Why I escalated:** Replacing the volume requires deleting PVC `data-ledger-queue-0`. Because the PV's reclaimPolicy is `Delete`, that action will also destroy the PV object and the AOF data on the disk — permanently losing buffered settlement messages — *before* the infra team has confirmed the node is gone for good. That is an irreversible financial data-loss decision that must be made by an authorised engineer, not automated away.
